candidate_relations.label: Primary Hyperparathyroidism, unmanaged
candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is a three-part composite: brown tumor (the histopathologically confirmed finger lesion) secondary to primary hyperparathyroidism caused specifically by parathyroid carcinoma. C001 captures only the middle component (primary hyperparathyroidism, unmanaged) and neither names the brown tumor nor specifies parathyroid carcinoma as the etiology, despite the markedly elevated PTH (380 pmol/L, ~55× upper limit) and cervical nodule on sestamibi scintigraphy strongly suggesting malignancy.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Identifies the underlying endocrine disorder but omits the brown tumor (the presenting lesion and final diagnostic object), the specific etiology of parathyroid carcinoma, and the composite nature of the full benchmark diagnosis.

case_quality_flags: Extremely elevated PTH (380 pmol/L vs. reference 1.6–6.9 pmol/L) and cervical nodule on sestamibi scintigraphy support parathyroid carcinoma as the etiology, which is a required component of the benchmark but absent from the sole candidate.
Histopathology description (fibrous tissue, woven bone, osteoclast-like giant cells, brown cysts) is classic for brown tumor, also absent from the candidate.
